requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Fixes the generator/analyzer crash on closed generic value types from referenced assemblies. Two diagnostic sites in TypeCollector stop indexing `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` (lines 985 and 1077). The analyzer's diagnostic callback is now wrapped in a filter that silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source location inside the current compilation. Three tests compile a library to metadata and check that the consuming project builds with no diagnostics and gets a resolver. README and MsgPack004 docs describe the new 'reported by the defining assembly' policy.
story.why: The issue reports IndexOutOfRangeException (CS8785/AD0001) because metadata symbols have no syntax references. As a result, no resolver was generated and trimmed/AOT apps broke at runtime.
touches_beyond_requirement: A blanket filter on every analyzer diagnostic, not only the ones for metadata types. It drops any diagnostic with Location.None or an out-of-compilation location (line 239, lines 1444-1450).
A new documented policy, in README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md, that diagnostics for referenced types are not reported to the consumer.
story.confidence_overview: High that the two edited sites no longer throw for metadata properties. Medium that all crash sites are covered: the issue names three indexed sites, and the diff changes only two, so a third (issue line 735) may still exist outside the visible hunks. Medium that the tests run the analyzer as well as the generator; this depends on the repo's CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier configuration, which is not shown. The diagnostic-suppression filter is a policy choice broader than the crash fix.

MemberNeedsKey now uses item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), yielding null (Location.None) instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException on DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] for metadata members, which ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember exercises.

claims.text: When an analyzer report callback is supplied, every diagnostic goes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. A diagnostic is forwarded only if its location is in source and its tree belongs to the current compilation; all others, including Location.None, are dropped. A null callback (generator path) stays null.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

breaker.reason: Lines 239 and 1444-1450 of TypeCollector.cs wrap a non-null reportAnalyzerDiagnostic in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation and keep null as null, dropping Location.None and locations outside this.compilation. However, the diff alone cannot verify (1) that no other constructor or call site bypasses the private constructor at line 236, (2) that the generator path passes null for reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, or (3) that ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember actually executes ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, because VerifyCS is CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator> (GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 7) whose definition is not in the diff (standard CSharpSourceGeneratorTest runs no DiagnosticAnalyzers unless GetDiagnosticAnalyzers is overridden, and line 653 only runs MessagePackGenerator).

claims.text: The test helper separately runs the generator driver on the consuming compilation. It asserts there are no warning-or-higher diagnostics (this would catch CS8785-style generator exceptions) and that the expected resolver hint name is among the generated sources.

breaker.reason: Checked GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 650-659 and all three test methods calling RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync. The helper runs CSharpGeneratorDriver directly on usageCompilation, asserts no warning-or-higher diagnostics (which catches CS8785 on generator exceptions), and asserts expectedResolverHintName is present in GeneratedSources.

claims.text: Scope: the change adds no public API, no new analyzer rule descriptors and no reader/writer changes. The docs added in README and MsgPack004.md only describe the policy that consumers do not see diagnostics for referenced types.

breaker.reason: Checked all four changed files. No public APIs, analyzer descriptors, or serialization reader/writer calls were added or modified, and README.md lines 1639-1642 plus doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md lines 48-52 only document using closed generic types from referenced assemblies and the policy that member diagnostics are reported by the defining project.

refusals.what: Global suppression of analyzer diagnostics that lack an in-compilation source location.
refusals.why: It changes user-visible analyzer behavior for all diagnostics, not just metadata types. Dropping diagnostics for referenced types is a policy decision the requirement did not ask for; it only asked for no crash and a generated resolver.

refusals.what: Documentation committing to a new analyzer reporting policy.
refusals.why: The added docs promise behavior (diagnostics only in the defining project) beyond the requirement. Maintainers should confirm this is the intended product decision.

findings.description: Claim C4 disputed: Over-citation of GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 582-626 (ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember). C4's text describes only the plain struct and exact record struct trigger tests (lines 499-580), yet cites lines 499-648 and is the only claim citing lines 582-626 without mentioning that this third test puts an invalid unkeyed public property (public int Unkeyed at line 603) into the referenced assembly and asserts zero consumer diagnostics. Additionally, line 637's comment that VerifyCS.Test runs the analyzers depends on CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier outside the diff.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation's source, not just those for metadata types. Any existing diagnostic for a source-declared type that ends up with Location.None will now be silently suppressed. Examples: a GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation helper returning null, or a diagnostic intentionally created without a location. That is a regression in analyzer coverage that no test checks.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (its lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff changes only two (new lines 985 and 1077). If a third direct index remains elsewhere in GetObjectInfo, it can still crash for metadata types on a code path the new tests do not reach (e.g., fields or constructors).

The claim that this run exercises the analyzer (AD0001) depends on CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator> registering MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer, which is not visible in the diff. If it does not, the AD0001 half of the bug is untested.

The unkeyed-member test asserts only that no diagnostic appears. It does not check what the consumer-side generated formatter does with the unkeyed member of the metadata struct, so silently suppressing MsgPack004 could hide incorrect generated code.

REQ-2283 identified three DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites inside GetObjectInfo (lines 735, 1009, 1101 in v3.1.8). Accounting for the 24-line offset in current TypeCollector.cs (1009 -> 985, 1101 -> 1077), this change fixed only two of them and left the site around line 711 untouched. If a referenced generic value type lacks [MessagePackObject], or is closed in the consuming assembly with an unattributed type argument (e.g. MyGenericStruct<UnattributedType>, where GetObjectInfo passes the metadata member symbol as callerSymbol into CollectCore -> GetObjectInfo), indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] on a metadata symbol will still throw IndexOutOfRangeException.

When a valid generic [MessagePackObject] struct in a referenced assembly has a member of type T (such as [Key(0)] public T Content { get; set; }) and the consuming assembly closes T with an unformattable type (MyGenericStruct<NotFormattable>), the defining assembly cannot report any diagnostic on open T, while in the consuming assembly GetObjectInfo walks the metadata member symbol and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops any diagnostic whose location is not in the consuming compilation's syntax trees. Neither project reports the error, contradicting README.md line 1642.

Adjacent to the fixed line 1077, line 1076 still evaluates derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation() unconditionally before checking member accessibility or whether reportDiagnostic is null. Because nullable annotations are enabled and GetLocation() is invoked without null-conditional access, GetSyntax returns a non-nullable SyntaxNode; if derivedKeyAttribute is an AttributeData on a metadata member (where ApplicationSyntaxReference is null), GetSyntax will throw when a referenced generic struct member uses a custom KeyAttribute subclass.
